tier_reason: There is no app to render. This repo is a library and nothing else: no bin/, no exe/, no server, no CLI entry point, no gemspec - grep for a main, a Rack app or an executable finds nothing. lib/scheduling is loaded by a caller with -Ilib, so there is no process to start and no URL to point a browser at, which is why run and app_url are null. Everything short of that works and was run here: bundle install resolves 16 gems into vendor/bundle, the minitest suite reports 5 runs, 8 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips, the coverage run reports the same 5 runs and writes lcov for both library files, and RuboCop writes SARIF over all four Ruby files.

commands.install: RB=$(ls -d /opt/hostedtoolcache/Ruby/3.3.*/x64/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); export PATH="${RB:-$(dirname "$(command -v bundle)")}:$PATH"; bundle config set --local path vendor/bundle && bundle install
commands.test: RB=$(ls -d /opt/hostedtoolcache/Ruby/3.3.*/x64/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); export PATH="${RB:-$(dirname "$(command -v bundle)")}:$PATH"; bundle exec ruby -Ilib -e 'files = Dir.glob("test/**/test_*.rb").sort; abort("no test files matched test/**/test_*.rb") if files.empty?; files.each { |f| require File.expand_path(f) }'
commands.coverage:
RB=$(ls -d /opt/hostedtoolcache/Ruby/3.3.*/x64/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); export PATH="${RB:-$(dirname "$(command -v bundle)")}:$PATH"; set -e
mkdir -p vendor/coverage
printf 'eval_gemfile "%s/Gemfile"\ngem "simplecov", "~> 0.22"\ngem "simplecov-lcov", "~> 0.8"\n' "$PWD" > vendor/coverage/Gemfile
cat > vendor/coverage/run.rb <<'COVERAGE_RUNNER'
# Written by commands.coverage; not part of the repo.
require "simplecov"
require "simplecov-lcov"

SimpleCov::Formatter::LcovFormatter.config do |config|
  config.report_with_single_file = true
  config.single_report_path = "vendor/coverage/lcov.info"
end

# simplecov-lcov writes "SF:./lib/x.rb"; the gate matches SF paths against
# git's changed-file list, which has no "./" prefix, so strip it.
class RepoRelativeLcov
  def format(result)
    SimpleCov::Formatter::LcovFormatter.new.format(result)
    path = File.join(SimpleCov.root, "vendor/coverage/lcov.info")
    File.write(path, File.read(path).gsub(/^SF:\.\//, "SF:"))
  end
end

SimpleCov.formatter = RepoRelativeLcov
SimpleCov.start do
  # Without this SimpleCov drops .resultset.json into ./coverage, which is not
  # in .gitignore; everything the sandbox writes belongs under vendor/.
  coverage_dir "vendor/coverage"
  add_filter "/test/"
  add_filter "/vendor/"
  track_files "lib/**/*.rb"
end

# The same tests commands.test runs, loaded in one process so one report
# covers all of them.
files = Dir.glob("test/**/test_*.rb").sort
abort("no test files matched test/**/test_*.rb") if files.empty?
files.each { |f| require File.expand_path(f) }
COVERAGE_RUNNER
export BUNDLE_GEMFILE="$PWD/vendor/coverage/Gemfile" BUNDLE_PATH="$PWD/vendor/bundle"
bundle install
bundle exec ruby -Ilib vendor/coverage/run.rb

dropped.what: uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1 with ruby-version: "3.3" and bundler-cache: true
dropped.why: A GitHub Action cannot run inside the sandbox, which executes plain shell commands. What it provides is carried across by other means rather than ignored: the Ruby version by selecting a 3.3.x from the runner's tool cache in the install and test commands, and the gem cache by installing into vendor/bundle. Only the Action itself is dropped.

dropped.what: the second step, bundle exec rubocop
dropped.why: Superseded by the static_checks entry, and the round-1 reason for dropping it was wrong. It said the factory's static gate already runs RuboCop against per-file baselines; the gate does have a native RuboCop, but on this runner it cannot run ("bundler: command not found: rubocop"), so nothing was being counted at all. RuboCop is still not the build command - this repo has nothing to build, and a bare `bundle exec rubocop` as the build would fail the trial on the first pre-existing offense instead of ratcheting it. It runs as a declared static check instead. It passes here: 4 files inspected, no offenses detected.

dropped.what: the bare bundle install in the Test section
dropped.why: Kept, but not verbatim. Run as written it fails on this runner with Bundler::ReadOnlyFileSystemError against the shared gem home, so the sandbox sets a local install path first. The README describes a developer's machine, where the gem home is writable; the difference is environment, not intent.

dropped.what: adding simplecov and simplecov-lcov to the repo's own Gemfile
dropped.why: The repo has no coverage tool, and the gates need an lcov report. Editing the Gemfile is the obvious way and was deliberately not taken: setup's changes to the repo are not kept, so a Gemfile edit would vanish and the coverage command would then fail on every PR. Instead commands.coverage writes vendor/coverage/Gemfile, which eval_gemfile's the repo's own Gemfile and adds the two gems, and resolves it with BUNDLE_GEMFILE. Everything it writes is under vendor/, which .gitignore already ignores, so the tree stays clean. The cost is that the coverage gems are not pinned in a committed lockfile; they are constrained to simplecov ~> 0.22 and simplecov-lcov ~> 0.8.

exercised: The whole of lib/scheduling: Slot (half-open overlaps?, minutes, to_s, the ArgumentError on a slot that does not end after it starts) and Calendar (book, free?, booked_minutes, gaps, and the Calendar::Conflict error), loaded with ruby -Ilib.

The entire test suite — test/test_calendar.rb is the only test file — at 5 runs and 8 assertions, covering both decisions the README says a change could quietly reverse: back-to-back bookings do not clash, and an overlap raises naming the clash rather than returning false.
The exact message Calendar#book raises, since test_an_overlap_raises_naming_the_clash asserts the clashing slot's HH:MM-HH:MM form appears in it.
Gap computation across the leading, interior and trailing gaps of a day (test_gaps_between_bookings).

Dependency resolution from the Gemfile with no lockfile committed: bundle install resolves minitest and rubocop afresh within their ~> constraints, so a resolution that breaks the build shows up here.

RuboCop over all four Ruby files with the repo's own .rubocop.yml, including Style/Documentation and the double-quote style. Run during this episode with no offenses. It is the static gate's command rather than the manifest's, but it needs nothing the sandbox does not already provide.

Line coverage of lib/, measured by SimpleCov and written as lcov at vendor/coverage/lcov.info: 35 relevant lines across the two library files, 34 covered (97.1%), the one miss being Calendar#free? at calendar.rb:30, which no test calls. The gate's diff coverage can therefore be measured on any change to lib/.

RuboCop over all four Ruby files with the repo's own .rubocop.yml, written as SARIF at vendor/static/rubocop.sarif via RuboCop's built-in sarif formatter. Verified to count: a scratch file with three deliberate offenses produced three SARIF results with cop names (Style/Documentation, Lint/UselessAssignment, Style/StringLiterals) and repo-relative paths; the repo as it stands produces none.

not_exercised.what: Anything that requires starting a process: a server, a CLI, an HTTP request, a rendered page, a screenshot, a browser flow.
not_exercised.why: This repo contains no executable of any kind. The limit is the repo's, not the sandbox's — there is nothing here that could be started. A change that adds a bin/ or a server is the signal to amend this manifest, because the tier would then be able to reach renders.

not_exercised.what: Behaviour under any Ruby other than the single 3.3.x the runner's tool cache happens to provide, and under any dependency versions other than the ones resolved on the day.
not_exercised.why: CI pins ruby-version 3.3 and .rubocop.yml sets TargetRubyVersion: 3.3, so the sandbox selects a 3.3.x to match — 3.3.13 when measured. There is no version matrix anywhere in the repo, so neither CI nor the sandbox says anything about other versions. Note the fallback: if no 3.3.x is in the tool cache the commands use whichever Ruby owns bundle, which on this runner is 4.0.9; the tests pass there too, but that path is a fallback, not the measured configuration.

not_exercised.what: Time types other than ::Time, and time zone or DST behaviour.
not_exercised.why: Slot is duck-typed — it only needs endpoints that compare, subtract and answer strftime — but every test builds them with Time.parse at a fixed date in UTC. Nothing here exercises a DateTime, an ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone, a local zone, or a day on which the clocks change. A change to how Slot handles its endpoints is not covered by what passes here.

not_exercised.what: Concurrency, persistence and anything outliving the process.
not_exercised.why: A Calendar is an in-memory array with no locking and no store. Two threads booking at once, or a calendar surviving a restart, are outside both the code and the tests. Note that Calendar#slots hands back the live array, so a caller could mutate it past book — untested, and worth a deliberate decision rather than a quiet change.

book is a linear scan and re-sorts the whole array on every insert. The suite books at most two slots, so it would not notice a change that made this quadratic or worse. There is no benchmark in the repo.

not_exercised.what: Branch coverage, and coverage of the test files themselves.
not_exercised.why: SimpleCov is started in line mode with /test/ filtered out, so the report says which lines ran, not which branches. Slot#overlaps? is a single line with two comparisons: a change that broke one half of the half-open rule would still show the line as covered. Diff coverage is a floor, not a proof.

not_exercised.what: Any RuboCop cop that the repo's .rubocop.yml disables, and any cop from a rubocop extension gem.
not_exercised.why: The SARIF comes from the repo's own configuration, which is the point - it counts what this repo has decided to enforce. rubocop-minitest, rubocop-performance and rubocop-rake are not in the Gemfile, so their cops do not run, and NewCops: enable means a RuboCop upgrade can add cops and so add findings that no change caused.

The cause is two different Ruby installations: bundle resolves to the tool cache's Ruby 4.0.9 while ruby on PATH is /usr/bin/ruby 3.3.8, so bundle exec spawns an interpreter that cannot see gems installed under the other one's ABI directory. bundle exec rubocop was unaffected, because a binstub runs under bundler's own Ruby.

episode.tried: Amendment round. Read amend.json (owner, coverage-and-checkers), then read the factory runner itself rather than guessing what the gates expect: how bsf gates coverage parses a report (readCoverage/fromLcov: per-file LF/LH, paths resolved with rel(root, ...)), how bsf gates tests chooses its command (commands.coverage instead of commands.test when set), and which checkers the static gate already runs natively.
episode.observed: Three things that decided the design. fromLcov keys files by rel(root, path), and rel leaves a relative path untouched - so an "SF:./lib/x.rb" line would never match git's "lib/x.rb" and diff coverage would silently find nothing. The tests gate runs commands.coverage in place of commands.test, so the coverage run has to be the tests, not a second suite. And the static gate does have a native RuboCop, triggered by Gemfile + .rubocop.yml.

static_checks.name: rubocop
static_checks.command: RB=$(ls -d /opt/hostedtoolcache/Ruby/3.3.*/x64/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); export PATH="${RB:-$(dirname "$(command -v bundle)")}:$PATH"; mkdir -p vendor/static && bundle exec rubocop --format sarif --out vendor/static/rubocop.sarif --force-exclusion
static_checks.why: RuboCop is the only checker this repo runs, and the factory's own native RuboCop cannot run here. Measured: `bsf gates static` reports "rubocop - bundler: command not found: rubocop" and concludes neutral, because it invokes a bare `bundle exec rubocop` with the job's PATH, where `bundle` is the tool cache's Ruby 4.0.9 bundler while the install puts the gems under Ruby 3.3's ABI directory. Installing them for 4.0.9 as well is not a way out: its bundler re-execs the lockfile's bundler 2.5.22, which dies on Ruby 4 with "undefined method 'parse' for class CGI". This entry runs the same RuboCop with the same .rubocop.yml, under the Ruby 3.3 the rest of the sandbox uses, and writes RuboCop's own built-in SARIF - the same cop names the native tool would report, so the per-file baselines mean the same thing. Expect the gate's summary to go on listing rubocop under "Tools that could not run": that is the native attempt, and it does not decide the conclusion - measured with this manifest, the gate prints "Ran: rubocop" and conclusion=success. If the runner image ever lets the native tool run, both would count the same offenses and the ratchet would fail loudly; drop this entry then.

amended_by: owner/coverage-and-checkers (2026-11-21): the coverage gate reported no coverage report on every PR, so diff coverage was never measured, and the static gate counted nothing. Answered with commands.coverage + coverage_report (SimpleCov -> lcov) and a static_checks entry that runs the repo's own RuboCop to SARIF.
